title: Exploratory study - Measurement of postoperative physical activity in smokers after implantation of total knee or total hip arthroplasty.
summary:
It is known that smoking is harmful in several ways. It also interferes with wound healing and can lead to complications after surgery. In principle, it is recommended to stop smoking in the period around surgical procedures.
After elective orthopedic surgery such as knee (KTEP) or total hip arthroplasty (HTEP) implantation, it is important to become mobile quickly. It has been observed, but not scientifically evaluated, that smokers often become mobile faster after such surgery just to be able to smoke (in designated areas).
This study will now compare the outcomes of the two groups of patients (smokers and non-smokers) with KTEP or HTEP. 
Activity levels and pain medication consumption will be compared. After inclusion in the study project, the study patients will receive a pedometer with which they will record the steps taken daily and document them in a step diary.
